obtained.how: Wayback Machine capture (23 July 2018) of the publisher's free PDF on pnas.org (PNAS back content is free to read); PMC's own PDF (PMC427100) returned a bot-check page and was not used

bibliography.checked_against: Crossref and the article's first page
bibliography.corrections: drop '(abstract only.)' from the reference note and '(abstract only)' from §3.8.4: the full text is free and was read. Otherwise the entry agrees: Botkin, D. B., Jordan, P. A., Dominski, A. S., Lowendorf, H. S. & Hutchinson, G. E. 1973. Sodium dynamics in a northern ecosystem. PNAS 70(10): 2745–2748 (October 1973).

claims.location: p. 2745 (PDF p. 1), Abstract and text; p. 2746 (PDF p. 2), Table 1
claims.quote: submerged and floating leaved water-plants are relatively rich
claims.conditions: Isle Royale, Lake Superior; sodium in submerged and floating aquatics ≈ 500-fold, and in emergents and hygrophytes ≈ 50-fold, that of the island's terrestrial plants; browse averages 10 ppm Na; summer aquatic feeding 'would provide an adequate source, if the animal can store the element'
claims.note: An estimate, not a measured sodium budget: the herd's need is put at 243 kg/yr; browse eaten would supply only 7–14 % of it; aquatic production at ≥ 500 ppm might hold ~2,500 kg, about 10 times the need (p. 2747).

claims.claim: leaves supply energy (Belovsky 1981; Botkin et al. 1973)
claims.note: Botkin et al. say nothing about energy. They state only that browse (current leaves and twigs, some bark) is about 90 % of the moose's annual intake and is very poor in sodium. The energy half of the sentence must rest on Belovsky 1981 alone.

tried.note: PMC landing page only (a scanned-article record; kept briefly, replaced by the PDF)

notes: Other values: moose on Isle Royale feed extensively on aquatic macrophytes for about 8 weeks in summer; sodium at the mud licks averages 24 ppm; aquatic plants' chloride exceeds their sodium, so they also supply NaCl. Table 1 gives sodium (ppm, dry) by species (e.g. Nuphar, Potamogeton, Chara) but its layout is jumbled in the text layer: read it on the page image before using any value.
